newsitem.title: FRANCE: New boardroom protest at Credit Foncier.
newsitem.headline: New boardroom protest at Credit Foncier.

text.p: Angry employees held the governor and several executives of Credit Foncier de France inside the French bank's headquarters on Friday, in a new protest about plans to wind the venerable property lender down, union officials said.

The workers are fighting a plan to wind down the company and spin its housing loans business off to another group called Credit Immobilier, a plan the government calls unavoidable. A union official involved in the protest said the bank's governor, Jerome Meysonnier, told the demonstrators the bank could be kept alive as a going concern.
"Meyssonnier told us Credit Foncier is viable and there are solutions other than Credit Immobilier," he said.
A bank official said this account was essentially correct.

Meyssonnier, appointed by the government, appears to be at odds with the finance ministry over the bank's future and recently forecast it could make a profit of a billion francs this year after the 10.8 billion 1995 loss that triggered the wind-down plan.

Finance minister Jean Arthuis said on Wednesday he would present legislation for the second stage of the plan to spin off Credit Foncier into a new state company and its housing loans portfolio to Credit Immobilier.
Friday's boardroom incident was one of many protests since it became apparent Credit Foncier was heading for closure.
